Itch.io link:
https://woootbm.itch.io/automatic-messiah
​
Content warning: features profanity, violence, and sometimes touches dark themes (fascism, sadism, slavery, etc.) due to post-apocalyptic setting.
You are an ambassador from a distant solar system. Your mission is to establish diplomatic relations with a primitive planet called "Earth." After your hundred-year journey you arrive to find that the world has been destroyed.
Now you must explore this wasteland and try to finish the job... one way or the other.
Spoiler:
Screenshots
Announcement:
This (0.4.x) will be the last of the public builds. After this, I will be having a closed "beta" during either 0.5.x or 0.6.x that will require sign-ups.
Not only that,
but during these closed beta tests I will be offering a (small) compensation to those who fill out provided feedback forms!
Slots will be limited, so keep a look out for that!
Features:
Strategic turn-based combat with different player builds.
Fight using either lethal, non-lethal, or diplomatic methods and change how the world perceives your character as well as unlocking different skills based on your path.
A large, interconnected map with non-linear exploration
(current available content not reflective of this)
.
3 difficulty settings and generous auto-save for a more modern experience.
An objective system that both guides the player on the main path and provides side quest distractions.
CURRENT STATE:
v0.4.3
Early pre-alpha! Only three areas with three dungeons and one city hub.
Known issues:
Mouse movement frequently has pathing issues
Controller supported but is not recommended due to missing functions.
If so inclined, I have made a
feedback form
for players who wish to give their thoughts!
https://forms.gle/YLJy3VJSC2W7A66y6
You can also go straight to the comments if you like;
all feedback is welcome!
Please leave a rating on the Itch page. Good or bad, I think those help with visibility (and it's useful feedback for me from folks who don't wanna type a bunch of stuff).

posts.body:
I never even replied to his post sharing my stream!
I thought I would share some additional thoughts. It's been a few days since streaming it, so not everything is quite so fresh in my mind.
First of all, I know this sounds silly, but I think you should leave in the number of characters players can insert for names, and actually if possible, allow for more characters. I can totally understand that by doing that the end result looks a little bit less polished with names overlapping UI elements, but the amount of fun I had with MMMMMMMMMMMM just can't be understated. And obviously Tony having fun with it too. It's so small, but yet, in these types of games, I really think giving your character a whacky name gives this subtle boost in enjoyability.
I suppose in an ideal world, you would have a set character limit, but maybe have a button the player can click to disable the character limit, but show a pop up "May cause text to overlap in the UI!". But that obviously would require comissioning a programmer to fix that, and I don't know if it's worth the cost.
Side note; I said I stole the joke from another, more famous, youtuber.
Here is where that joke was stolen from.
(Also, not him using MMMMMM but this quote here sums up my feelings,
"it's not a bug, it's perfection."
)
On a similar note, I think it would be great if you could also give the fabricator a name as well. I mean, why not?
As far as combat goes, I think Tony hit on a lot of stuff in his coverage of your game. Most of the problems come down to UX/UI stuff.
The other thing is the difficulty, and the difficulty curve itself. Iirc, the regular battles felt easy. It was just the one boss mob that was tough, but only tough because he felt unfair. I had defeated him and he healed himself and respawned himself. All that felt like BS.
The battle fatigue did start to weight on me by the end. I think this is made more apparent by not being able to deal damage with the other party members; you wind up having to wait and/or waste their turns just to deal some damage with MMMMMMMM.
Anyways, those are just some thoughts. I think I already mentioned a lot of these in my video and the google form.
I just wanted to bump this thread because: yo, folks:
PLAY. THIS. GAME!
​

posts.author: hiddenone
posts.body:
I gave your demo a go, and I've watched a few of your reviews so I won't hold back on my feedback.
Spoiler:
The feedback
First issue I ran into was on the title screen, the game autostarts in fullscreen. That's fine for some people, but it makes it tough to take notes or jump to a different window to check something. If you're going to include fullscreen, please make sure there's an easy way to turn it off in the options menu.
When it came to choosing a difficulty I think changing how the difficulties are worded would be good, since right now Normal mode states enemy health is lowered and Tactical has unchanged health. I'm sure that's because of a plugin for the health, but I don't think you have to actually tell players that enemies are weaker in Normal mode. They don't know what the default health is, so you could say that Normal has a normal amount of health and Tactical has increased health. That would make Tactical feel more like a challenge instead of the 'default' difficulty.
The intro sets the scene well, and the use of placeholder images was smart even if the people's faces on the ai art were horrific. I do want to suggest a small edit to the Ambassador's intro image: remove its belly button. It's a tiny detail, but not having a belly button can trigger our "that's not a person" instinct and will make it seem even more robotic. It would have also been nice if I had some options on how the Ambassador responds in the intro instead of waiting until after the fight with Jooey's goons, just to help set up its personality early on.
The dirty and desolate exterior map does sell the post-apocalyptic setting, but it felt a bit too familiar to me. I know you're taking inspiration from Fallout and games like it, but it would be interesting if there was still vegetation around. Humans may have mostly died off, but that doesn't mean that plants have, especially if the nuclear destruction was a while ago. Lush green fields of grass may not quite fit the post-apocalypse style you're going for, but what about mutated cacti or ivy? Something to consider if you were trying to find ways to make the game stand out from other brown-toned apocalypses.
The controls worked well enough, I did get caught on some tiny things a points, but overall it was fine. I do think the movement plugin didn't want to play well with events though, since sometimes I had trouble interacting with a box I was pretty sure was in front of me and enemies would run away from me before circling back to attack. That made battles a little difficult to start, since I couldn't walk into them to start battle and had to wait until they bumped into me. I'm not sure how to fix that, but looking into a way to make the events 'smarter' in regards to interacting would make exploring maps more enjoyable.
Battles are where I had the most fun and also got the most annoyed. I started on Casual difficulty but after a few easy fights with the dogs I switched to Tactical for a more interesting challenge. Enemies being able to call for reinforcements was a neat effect, but it felt like it happened a bit too often in battles. I would have preferred the enemies to appear right off the bat sometimes instead of always waiting a turn or two to show up, since that would change how I approached the battles. Since I knew it was likely another enemy would appear later, I ended up saving my stronger attacks just in case I needed it, leading to sometimes longer battles than they should have been. Though I do get that that's mostly because of my playstyle.
Having a single damage dealer with two supporters is a neat idea and it worked pretty well, but I do wish that Fabricator could use the Grenade instead of just making it. It may change later in the game, but in the demo I rarely had enough enemies to make giving up a turn of healing or a Barbs of Light worthwhile to make a grenade. Speaking of Barbs of Light, did you mean for it to be so powerful? It was pretty much a necessity in battles, since it was the only other way to damage enemies when it wasn't Ambassador's turn. So instead of playing around with Fabricator's other skills I found myself mostly focusing on using Barbs of Light and then recovering its Battery so I could heal or recast it.
Computer's Scan skill was one of my most-used skills, though I think you should adjust where the weakness appears because sometimes it blended into the background or ended up hidden behind the name popup window when selecting a target. For the most part I didn't use Predict because its other skills were more useful to my playstyle, if it also decreased enemy defense slightly I would have been more likely to use it. The Delay Pattern skill was extremely useful once I got it, and made a few battles a piece of cake since I could pair it up with Adrenaline to destroy strong enemies before they could attack. I don't know if it balances out more later, but that skill may need a short wait between uses or cost at least 10 Battery so Computer's other skills that do have a cost don't seem lesser in comparison.
The tips gained from hovering over enemy states were super useful, but I wish there was a key press option to see them instead of using the mouse. I prefer to play rm games with the keyboard only or mouse only and in this case having to use both was really the only option. I also am curious if there's a way to get rid of Septic Contamination, because it was doing 30 damage to me every turn and lasted the whole battle. If there was a skill that cured it, even if it caused Ambassador to lose a turn of attacking it could make for some difficult but interesting decisions. Overall battles were fun enough that I went out of my way to battle every enemy. I just wish that they dropped equipment or other items so I could have seen how those could change battles.
I had major issues with the lockpicking minigame because of one dumb reason: I play games with the sound off to avoid headaches. Since I couldn't hear the tumbler noise cue and couldn't open the menu, I was trapped in the tutorial minigame and had to reload to avoid testing every combination to beat it. It would be very helpful for your players who play without sound (or can't hear the sound) if there was a visual cue like a burst of sparks or the tumbler glows for a moment when it's in the right spot. The lockpicking controls themselves were a little finicky too, for the minigame it may be better to stick with grid movement or limit the player to only moving to the spots right under the tumblers.
In the police station I ran into some framerate issues (dropping to and staying below 20 repeatedly), which led to some jerky movements. I'm not sure if it was caused by your lighting plugin or another event, but you should look into that. The darkness itself made seeing the zombies on the map and in battles difficult as well, I don't know if you wanted your zombies to blend in with the battlebacks but it took away from their scariness to me since I could just see blobs to attack.
A small thing I'd like to see changed with the mapping is to have more of edges visible if there are events near them, especially where the window was on the second floor. I didn't realize there was a window there at first, and if I could see the whole thing I would have been able to guess what was coming. Personally that would've made that whole scene better.
Bugs/Errors:
⦁    After choosing the Remorse option after the intro fight, Ambassador's dialogue is green like Computer's (not positive if this is a bug or not, but seemed odd)
⦁    Can walk on the blue tiles in the base, making me able to stand on the edge of the ceiling
⦁    The debug barrel: I found a barrel in the center of the town area keeps giving me things even though it doesn't have a green highlight. Might want to move that off to a side, unless you wanted people to find it easily
⦁    Can walk close enough to roof of building near police station that Ambassador can stand partly on the roof
And I think that's about it. Overall, you're definitely hitting that Fallout vibe, which is great if that's what you're aiming for. But I think you can do even better, so why not play around a bit and give your game even more of your own unique spin?
No matter what you decide, I'm looking forward to seeing more of this game so good luck!

Don't do this
It's a parallel event checking region right? I think in the past you explained to me that's how you accomplished it.
0 wait frames causes the event to be checked wait too frequently and will cause performance problems. 3 - 5 for this specific event is probably the lowest you can go.
For all parallel events,
A wait frame of 1 is going to give the biggest performance boost, with that gain falling off quickly there after. I'd say beyond a wait frame of 5 you begin to get severe diminishing returns, and at 20 it's not making any sort of difference really, but it still gives peace of mind that the event is (hopefully) performing well. Plus small performance costs add up over time! So by giving long wait frames where possible, you can rest assured they aren't adding much to the overall performance cost.
Wouldn't it be weird that selecting "hard mode" makes the game harder to run on some PCs? Lol

posts.author: woootbm
posts.body:
TheAM-Dol said:
Don't do this
It's a parallel event checking region right?
Click to expand...
No, don’t worry. I’ll start from the top. It’s yanfly region around the enemy event. Walking into the region flips a switch. This switch flips the event page to a parallel that waits 60 frames before going to the next page. The waiting page is for playing the ! Balloon and the aggro sound, giving the player time to react. The “next” page is the actual chase that had event touch to start the fight. The enemy’s chasing movement, resetting location and resetting switches is all done in the movement route of the chase page.
So when I say “wait 0 frames”, all that does is remove the buffer time between the aggroing and chasing pages of the same event. There is no constantly looping parallel.

Anyway, I beat the demo (I assume Crysdale is the end, took me around 5 hours), and thought it was pretty good. I do have some suggestions though.
What I Like
I really like the world design so far. The slang, the use of bullets as currency, and the fact that humans are concentrated in one area make it more unique than your usual Mad Max clone.
The map design is nice, no complaints there.
The main character is believable and acts like they should, a naive newcomer to a post apocalyptic society.
I like that combat doesn't drag, it resolves pretty quickly. Healing after battle is nice too.
The leader of Crysdale being kind of an assh*le was refreshing. Usually settlements are grateful for you saving their hide, like they were waiting for you to come along the entire time, but here the world exists seperate from you.
What I think can be Improved
There's a passability glitch here where you get stuck on the geometry and can't pass, I legitimately thought I got softlocked. I think it went away when I left the plant and went back inside.
The Light Wall skill seems underpowered. It's nice when fighting against the dogs but when you have a crowd of enemies it disappears fast, I stopped using it early on for Barbs/Blades of Light and the occasional grenade.
I'm not sure what purpose non-lethal damage or Diplomacy serves beyond ending some encounters quicker. To me, it's basically the same as lethal damage and seems to have the same after battle effect of enemies being removed from the map, and scripted encounters running off. Maybe make them have separate effects, like scripted encounters dying to lethal damage vs running away?
I would make the dialogue choices show their full lines, as right now they are very "Fallout 4-y" and non-specific. I would like to know what my character is going to say before I choose it.
The green lettering for the Battery bar blends in, making it a bit harder to read. The font size is also a bit small.
The music could use some more variety. Its good, but gets very same-y after several hours.
Not sure of the logic behind the reload costs. For instance:
The Topson .45 (clearly based on an M1 Thompson) would either use 20 or 30 ammo per reload, as those are the standard magazine sizes for it.
The S1 Errand 30-06 (looks like an M1 Garand) should have a reload cost of 8 instead of 6.
the .387 Stallion should be 6 instead of 5.
the SxS Redding should be 2, but have a longer reload time than either the S1 or the Topson. Maybe have the same time as the .387?
I didn't use the Huntsman .308 or the Handshake, but the 308 would cost 5.

I played the demo (at least up to the point when I couldn't find a red marker that'd allow me to reach other areas, after solving the water plant case and informing the merchant of the cleared road block). Here's some thoughts:
The mapping seems nice for this kind of "Fallout" style game. Not sure what's supposed to be a placeholder and what's not, but the enemy battlers and map sprites work ok. My 5-year-old laptop suffers from big frame drops (even bigger in the battles) though, going to single digits at times (my GPU(?) setting might not be at full power). The map sprites also blink (load slowly?) when they change the sheet to do some action, which looks very amateurish/buggy. I would also personally use battlebacks in the fights.
These kinds of games would also benefit from large environments where you could explore freely, which is of course hard for a single dev to do. Right now you can easily check all the places and mindlessly collect everything. The story and writing seemed ok, but I was kind of missing some more NPCs and sidequests that had different paths/solutions.
I was playing on normal difficulty and the battles started easy, but the challenge rose nicely with each new area. At the end against the spiders I kind of felt that you needed to have some points in parry to have a fairer chance, but maybe that's just because I wasn't exploring all options. I like it that the game wasn't only about spamming attack, but I also found that in some situations it was kind of annoying having to work with the 2 non-attacking party members. Like if you were fighting a trash mob or if only a single enemy was remaining, it was kind of useless to use the computer/bot skills (and watch the animations etc). Maybe have a way to take them out of turn order with a button press? But yeah, I found use for many of the skills, like even the Computer one where it delays an enemy turn order. I was saved by that many times when I managed to finish off an enemy with a second strike before they managed to multi-attack me. And lastly, I think that the enemies could use more variety in how you have to deal with them. Might be just the way I was playing, but for me it was always just finishing the multi-hit-attackers with strong skills as fast as possible.
The lockpick minigame was ok, though some could see it only as a waste of time (if there's no breaking lockpics etc). Maybe there could be more button presses and you had to go forward and backward or something. The number minigames were too easy in the beginning (the one at the end was ok). Is it a design choice though that there are correct solutions that don't work (at least in the last one)?
Oh and lastly, I didn't like the mechanic were you could just leave the interaction and try again if you lacked charisma, and didn't have to fight. But maybe that's just for the demo?
Anyway, this is something different, and I could see it turning out good if you can sink a lot of time in it. Good luck with the project!

I’m not entirely sold on the pixel movement, it’s always so janky and such a hassle in RPG Maker, but I feel for this kind of mapping and game it would be a bonus if it was smoother and the pathfinding more polished than it is at this point. I did notice the less enemies on screen, because I killed them, the better the FPS would become.
I like the arrows telling me where the transfer events are but would personally prefer them to be player touch rather than action button. That could just be a me thing though. I also love the interactables/loot flashing green to let the player know what can be interacted with at a quick glance. I thought the lockpicking scene was pretty cool and original. It’s simple but it works. The “hacking” minigame is a little awkward and when Computer is facing up interacting with the top middle square, you can’t see the number, so I had to walk around to the side to see what I was doing. Maybe make Computer semi-transparent or use a smaller sprite to represent the player cursor or something.
On level up the Tip dialogue says: “All of the player’s damaging skills are increased by level.” Like a level, one level, 2 level, or… Also what does each attribute do? Most are self explanatory or intuitive but Efficiency isn’t and Charisma isn’t explained until a little later. Maybe lock upgrading attributes until the base is unlocked or give a quick summary of the attributes when the tip tells me to use my attribute points.
Mouse tracking for the quest log is kind of weird. I’m not sure how to explain it. Maybe it is because you have to select the available quests and then scroll to the active one and then click on it to view. Would be a lot cooler if it would just jump into the active ones from the get go.
After talking to Gim the first time and before fixing the terminator, the fps tanked to a solid 5 and stayed there until after shopping. The low fps and the pixel movement made interacting with the robot extremely difficult. It’s a little weird how I shopped at the Gim’s cart and then exited the shop scene and then was told by computer to buy the thing, meaning I had to interact with the cart and re-enter the shop scene. I love the opening to the base, very cool touch. After interacting with the sleeping pod thing and doing the tutorial, it continues to glow/flash green, so I interacted with it again and had to do the tutorial twice. Afterwards, I traveled west and the next map went into super low fps and that’s about where I stopped playing.
Some thoughts about fps. Does the pixel movement contribute to the low fps? Personally it wouldn’t be a deal breaker for me to not have it, although it would be preferred. Have you tried upgrading your nwjs? It can help with performance. You could also try indexing the colors on your parallax maps. It can greatly reduce their size, which reduces the load on the computer. You can lose some gradients and a little bit of detail but it’s more obvious over semi-transparent areas. Could be worth a shot.
Anywho, really cool game and concept. I’ve been following your progress for awhile and like the direction your game is heading.
